God's Judgments on the Priests, People, and Princes of Israel for Their Sins.</title> <div sID="gen22417" type="x-p"/> Judah, too, being guilty shall be punished; nor shall Assyria, whose aid they both sought, save them; judgments shall at last lead them to repentance.<div eID="gen22417" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22418" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12296"/><hi type="bold">1. the king--</hi>probably Pekah; the contemporary of Ahaz, king of Judah, under whom idolatry was first carried so far in Judah as to call for the judgment of the joint Syrian and Israelite invasion, as also that of Assyria.<div eID="gen22418" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22419" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">judgment is towards you--</hi>that is, threatens you from God.<div eID="gen22419" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22420" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">ye have been a snare on Mizpah ... net ... upon Tabor--</hi>As hunters spread their net and snares on the hills, Mizpah and Tabor, so ye have snared the people into idolatry and made them your prey by injustice. As Mizpah and Tabor mean a "watch tower," and a "lofty place," a fit scene for hunters, playing on the words, the prophet implies, in the lofty place in which I have set you, whereas ye ought to have been the watchers of the people, guarding them from evil, ye have been as hunters entrapping them into it [Jerome]. These two places are specified, Mizpah in the east and Tabor in the west, to include the high places throughout the whole kingdom, in which Israel's rulers set up idolatrous altars. <div eID="gen22420" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12297"/><div sID="gen22421" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12297"/><hi type="bold">2. revolters--</hi>apostates.<div eID="gen22421" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22422" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">profound--</hi>deeply rooted [Calvin] and sunk to the lowest depths, excessive in their idolatry (<reference osisRef="Hos.9.9">Ho 9:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.31.6">Is 31:6</reference>) [Henderson]. From the antithesis (<reference osisRef="Hos.5.3">Ho 5:3</reference>), "not hid from me," I prefer explaining, profoundly cunning in their idolatry. Jeroboam thought it a profound piece of policy to set up golden calves to represent God in Dan and Beth-el, in order to prevent Israel's heart from turning again to David's line by going up to Jerusalem to worship. So Israel's subsequent idolatry was grounded by their leaders on various pleas of state expediency (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.29.15">Is 29:15</reference>).<div eID="gen22422" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22423" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">to ... slaughter--</hi>He does not say "to sacrifice," for their so-called sacrifices were butcheries rather than sacrifices; there was nothing sacred about them, being to idols instead of to the holy God.<div eID="gen22423" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22424" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">though--</hi>Maurer translates, "and (in spite of their hope of safety through their slaughter of victims to idols) I will be a chastisement to them all." English Version is good sense: They have deeply revolted, notwithstanding all my prophetical warnings. <div eID="gen22424" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 2. revolters-- apostates. profound-- deeply rooted [Calvin] and sunk to the lowest depths, excessive in their idolatry ( Ho 9:9 ; Is 31:6 ) [Henderson]. From the antithesis ( Ho 5:3 ), "not hid from me," I prefer explaining, profoundly cunning in their idolatry. Jeroboam thought it a profound piece of policy to set up golden calves to represent God in Dan and Beth-el, in order to prevent Israel's heart from turning again to David's line by going up to Jerusalem to worship. So Israel's subsequent idolatry was grounded by their leaders on various pleas of state expediency (compare Is 29:15 ). to ... slaughter-- He does not say "to sacrifice," for their so-called sacrifices were butcheries rather than sacrifices; there was nothing sacred about them, being to idols instead of to the holy God. though-- Maurer translates, "and (in spite of their hope of safety through their slaughter of victims to idols) I will be a chastisement to them all." English Version is good sense: They have deeply revolted, notwithstanding all my prophetical warnings.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12299"/><div sID="gen22428" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12299"/><hi type="bold">4. They--</hi>Turning from a direct address to Ephraim, he uses the third person plural to characterize the people in general. The Hebrew is against the Margin, their doings will not suffer them" the omission of "them" in the Hebrew after the verb being unusual. The sense is, they are incurable, for they will not permit (as the Hebrew literally means) their doings to be framed so as to turn unto God. Implying that they resist the Spirit of God, not suffering Him to renew them; and give themselves up to "the spirit of whoredoms" (in antithesis to "the Spirit of God" implied in "suffer" or "permit") (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.12">Ho 4:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.63.10">Is 63:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.16.43">Eze 16:43</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.7.51">Ac 7:51</reference>). <div eID="gen22428" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12302"/><div sID="gen22434" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12302"/><hi type="bold">7. treacherously--</hi>as to the marriage covenant (<reference osisRef="Jer.3.20">Jr 3:20</reference>).<div eID="gen22434" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22435" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">strange children--</hi>alluding to "children of whoredoms" (<reference osisRef="Hos.1.2">Ho 1:2</reference>; 2:4). "Strange" or foreign implies that their idolatry was imported from abroad [Henderson]. Or rather, "regarded by God as strangers, not His," as being reared in idolatry. The case is desperate, when not only the existing, but also the rising, generation is reared in apostasy.<div eID="gen22435" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22436" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">a month--</hi>a very brief space of time shall elapse, and then punishment shall overtake them (<reference osisRef="Zech.11.8">Zec 11:8</reference>). The allusion seems to be to money loans, which were by the month, not as with us by the year. You cannot put it off; the time of your destruction is immediately and suddenly coming on you; just as the debtor must meet the creditor's demand at the expiration of the month. The prediction is of the invasion of Tiglath-pileser, who carried away Reuben, Gad, Naphtali, and the half tribe of Manasseh.<div eID="gen22436" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22437" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">portions--</hi>that is, possessions. Their resources and garrisons will not avail to save them. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12303"/><div sID="gen22438" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12303"/>8. The arrival of the enemy is announced in the form of an injunction to blow an alarm.<div eID="gen22438" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22439" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">cornet ... trumpet--</hi>The "cornet" was made of the curved horn of animals and was used by shepherds. The "trumpet" was of brass or silver, straight, and used in wars and on solemn occasions. The Hebrew is hatzotzerah, the sound imitating the trumpet note (<reference osisRef="Hos.8.1">Ho 8:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Num.10.2">Nu 10:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.4.5">Jr 4:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Joel.2.1">Joe 2:1</reference>).<div eID="gen22439" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22440" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Gibeah ... Ramah--</hi>both in Benjamin (<reference osisRef="Isa.10.29">Is 10:29</reference>).<div eID="gen22440" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22441" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Beth-aven--</hi>in Benjamin; not as in <reference osisRef="Hos.4.15">Ho 4:15</reference>; Beth-el, but a town east of it (<reference osisRef="Josh.7.2">Jos 7:2</reference>). "Cry aloud," namely, to raise the alarm. "Benjamin" is put for the whole southern kingdom of Judah (compare <reference osisRef="Hos.5.5">Ho 5:5</reference>), being the first part of it which would meet the foe advancing from the north. "After thee, O Benjamin," implies the position of Beth-aven, behind Benjamin, at the borders of Ephraim. When the foe is at Beth-aven, he is at Benjamin's rear, close upon thee, O Benjamin (<reference osisRef="Judg.5.14">Jud 5:14</reference>). <div eID="gen22441" type="x-p"/>

entries.reader_content_plain: 11. broken in judgment-- namely, the "judgment" of God on him ( Ho 5:1 ). walked after the commandment-- Jeroboam's, to worship the calves ( 2Ki 10:28-33 ). Compare Mi 6:16 , "the statutes of Omri," namely, idolatrous statutes. We ought to obey God rather than men ( Ac 5:29 ). Jerome reads "filthiness." The Septuagint gives the sense, not the literal translation: "after vanities."

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12307"/><div sID="gen22449" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12307"/><hi type="bold">12. as a moth--</hi>consuming a garment (<reference osisRef="Job.13.28">Job 13:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.39.11">Psa 39:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.50.9">Is 50:9</reference>).<div eID="gen22449" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22450" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Judah ... rottenness--</hi>Ephraim, or the ten tribes, are as a garment eaten by the moth; Judah as the body itself consumed by rottenness (<reference osisRef="Prov.12.4">Pr 12:4</reference>). Perhaps alluding to the superiority of the latter in having the house of David, and the temple, the religious center of the nation [Grotius]. As in <reference osisRef="Hos.5.13">Ho 5:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Hos.5.14">14</reference>, the violence of the calamity is prefigured by the "wound" which "a lion" inflicts, so here its long protracted duration, and the certainty and completeness of the destruction from small unforeseen beginnings, by the images of a slowly but surely consuming moth and rottenness. <div eID="gen22450" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12308"/><div sID="gen22451" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12308"/><hi type="bold">13. wound--</hi>literally, "bandage"; hence a bandaged wound (<reference osisRef="Isa.1.6">Is 1:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.30.12">Jr 30:12</reference>). "Saw," that is, felt its weakened state politically, and the dangers that threatened it. It aggravates their perversity, that, though aware of their unsound and calamitous state, they did not inquire into the cause or seek a right remedy.<div eID="gen22451" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22452" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">went ... to the Assyrian--</hi>First, Menahem (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.15.19">2Ki 15:19</reference>) applied to Pul; again, Hoshea to Shalmaneser (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.17.3">2Ki 17:3</reference>).<div eID="gen22452" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22453" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sent to King Jareb--</hi>Understand Judah as the nominative to "sent." Thus, as "Ephraim saw his sickness" (the first clause) answers in the parallelism to "Ephraim went to the Assyrian" (the third clause), so "Judah saw his wound" (the second clause) answers to (Judah) "sent to King Jareb" (the fourth clause). Jareb ought rather to be translated, "their defender," literally, "avenger" [Jerome]. The Assyrian "king," ever ready, for his own aggrandizement, to mix himself up with the affairs of neighboring states, professed to undertake Israel's and Judah's cause; in <reference osisRef="Judg.6.32">Jud 6:32</reference>, Jerub, in Jerub-baal is so used, namely, "plead one's cause." Judah, under Ahaz, applied to Tiglath-pileser for aid against Syria and Israel (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.16.7">2Ki 16:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Kgs.16.8">8</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Chr.28.16-2Chr.28.21">2Ch 28:16-21</reference>); the Assyrian "distressed him, but strengthened him not," fulfiling the prophecy here, "he could not heal you, nor cure you of your wound. <div eID="gen22453" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12310"/><div sID="gen22457" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12310"/><hi type="bold">15. return to my place--</hi>that is, withdraw My favor.<div eID="gen22457" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22458" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">till they acknowledge their offence--</hi>The Hebrew is, "till they suffer the penalty of their guilt." Probably "accepting the punishment of their guilt" (compare <reference osisRef="Zech.11.5">Zec 11:5</reference>) is included in the idea, as English Version translates. Compare <reference osisRef="Lev.26.40">Le 26:40</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.26.41">41</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.29.12">Jr 29:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.29.13">13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.6.9">Eze 6:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.20.43">20:43</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.36.31">36:31</reference>.<div eID="gen22458" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22459" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">seek my face--</hi>that is, seek My favor (<reference osisRef="Prov.29.26">Pr 29:26</reference>, Margin).<div eID="gen22459" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22460" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in ... affliction ... seek me early--</hi>that is, diligently; rising up before dawn to seek Me (<reference osisRef="Ps.119.147">Psa 119:147</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Ps.78.34">Psa 78:34</reference>). <chapter eID="Hos.5"/>
entries.content_plain: 15. return to my place-- that is, withdraw My favor. till they acknowledge their offence-- The Hebrew is, "till they suffer the penalty of their guilt." Probably "accepting the punishment of their guilt" (compare Zec 11:5 ) is included in the idea, as English Version translates. Compare Le 26:40 , 41 ; Jr 29:12 , 13 ; Eze 6:9 ; 20:43 ; 36:31 . seek my face-- that is, seek My favor ( Pr 29:26 , Margin). in ... affliction ... seek me early-- that is, diligently; rising up before dawn to seek Me ( Psa 119:147 ; compare Psa 78:34 ).
